_comment: Public surfaces this repo is responsible for, and how each is re-derived.
Three incidents share one shape: a guard or a public surface reporting
success without a non-empty, tip-locked inspection of the thing it
certifies. A counts workflow that had never executed. A build workflow
red from birth, so the page it generated was whatever was last committed
by hand. A site whose figures drift every time main moves. Two of those
were cross-repo: one repo wrote a number in prose and another parsed it,
which is an interface and was being maintained as prose.
Every surface below is checked by re-deriving the value from the tree and
comparing it to what the artifact actually says. A surface that inspects
nothing is a failure, not a pass. A peer repo that is absent is a failure,
not a skip, because 'could not look' reported as green is the same defect

Patterns are whitespace-tolerant on purpose. Markdown wraps prose, and a total split across a line break is still that total. A literal space here made this job silently skip the wrapped occurrence of the registry count and report CLEAN over a mutation that had applied.

The Pages site stopped publishing the doctor-check count in its 2026-08-14 portfolio redesign. That peer interface was retired here rather than forcing a removed UI statistic back onto the site just to satisfy an obsolete verifier. The registry pin and trap count remain live cross-repo contracts.

surfaces.why: the first screen a stranger reads
the doctor README publishes this count directly

peer_surfaces.why: the page pins the registry commit it was generated from; behind HEAD means stale
